title: Hamming Moving Average (HAMMA)
summary: A moving average weighted by the Hamming window, heaviest in the middle of the lookback and lightest at its two ends.
description:
The Hamming Moving Average weights the bars of its window with the Hamming taper, 0.54 - 0.46 * cos(2 * pi * k / (N - 1)), where k counts bars back from the newest and N is the window length. The weight is 0.08 at both ends of the window and rises to 1 in the middle, so the central bars dominate. The weighted prices are summed and divided by the sum of the weights.

The window grows with the chart until it holds `period` bars, with the weights rebuilt for each length. A window of a single bar weights that bar by one, so the line starts on the first bar at the price itself. A missing price is skipped with its weight, and a window with no usable weight falls back to the current price.
howToRead:
Read the HAMMA as a smooth trend line. Tapering the ends means a large bar entering or leaving the window moves the line gently rather than in a step, so its path is cleaner than a simple average of the same length. Because the weight sits in the middle of the window, the line runs roughly half a window behind price.

Use it for the direction and slope of the trend. It is slow to confirm a reversal, and a cross of price through the line comes after much of the move has happened.

settings.label: Period
settings.description: Number of bars in the full window. A longer period smooths more and lags more.

settings.label: Source
settings.description: The price series the average is taken from, the close by default.

faq.q: How does it differ from the Hanning average?
faq.a: Both use a cosine taper. The Hamming taper keeps a small weight of 0.08 at the ends of the window, while the Hanning taper falls all the way to zero.

faq.q: Why is the line smoother than a simple average?
faq.a: Bars enter and leave the window with small weights, so a single large bar shifts the line gradually instead of in one jump.
On the first bar. The window grows with the chart, and a one-bar window simply returns the price.
